message.reasoning_content:
Analyze this reduced C/C++ function. It may or may not contain a vulnerability.
Reply with single best line number where primary bug is introduced.

Plain char is signed, and ctype implementation indexes a table for values other than EOF.

Code:
while r < len
if s[r]=='%' && r+2 < len && isxdigit(s[r+1]) && isxdigit(s[r+2])
...
s[w++] = s[r++];

Bug: s is char*, but isxdigit expects unsigned char or EOF. With signed char, negative values cause out-of-bounds table index. So isxdigit(s[r+1]) uses signed char negative -> UB.

Also s[w++] writes in place, w may exceed? r increments, w increments same? For % case, w increments 1, r increments 3, so w <= r? Might be okay but in-place decode shrinks, so w <= r always. So no overflow.

Primary bug is isxdigit with signed char. Line 7 uses isxdigit(s[r+1]) and isxdigit(s[r+2]). Also line 6 uses s[r]=='%' fine.

Bug introduced at line 7? Or line 6? The call is on line 7. Might be both 7? The condition includes two calls. Smallest set: 7? Actually isxdigit appears twice on same line. Could be line 7.

Also s[r] used without cast. But isxdigit only problematic.

Answer: 7

If need both calls? line 7 covers both.

Return 7.
